fields.description: Issue dated April 28, 1928 (Vol. 6, no. 14) featuring editorials and commentary on Miami’s preparations for the forthcoming Shrine convention, including civic spending, expected visitors, and calls for hospitality. Includes pieces on keeping the Tamiami Trail free of advertising signs, traffic hazards on Biscayne Boulevard safety islands, and arguments against cutting the police force after the convention. Contains political satire and election-related content (including a platform advertisement), discussion of prohibition enforcement and liquor, local business and banking news (including Southern Bank & Trust Company reopening), transportation notes (bus line over the Tamiami Trail), and entertainment/coming events and advertisements.
